criterion: 4 — a Run link opens a cockpit terminal … an Anchor window, token-gated; 5 — a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged (Playwright screenshots)
message: Wave 2's Open link appends the page token the way the file link already does. Wave 6 then window.opens `/terminal?session=<sid>` and never mentions `token`. The W6.2 HOLD even asks whether the existing standalone page is reachable "with session+token as-is" — then the near-term URL drops the token. GET terminal transports are already 401-before-substance. He clicks Run ▶, a window opens, and it is blank. Criterion 4's Anchor window never appears; criterion 5's screenshot is an empty page. Carry the token the same way Open does. The alias is not the fix.

criterion: 5 — Nothing regresses, and it is seen — steward/cockpit nets stay green; a Gandalf run is opened from the plan outline AND the deliverables tile; a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged (Playwright screenshots)
message: The only machine-countable ship gate names `tests/test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`, a file no wave creates. It omits every new file the waves actually ship: the W1 containment stub gate, the W3 registrar/concurrency/round-trip tests, the W5/W6 Run-terminal tests, and the W7 Playwright file (`importorskip('playwright')` even if someone adds it). Foreman can go green on three old nets plus a missing path while the outline click-through, the Run window, and the hostile-Where fixtures never run. Criterion 5 is a claim about John's page. A gate that cannot see that page is how a green branch ships a dead click.

criterion: 1 — When a Gandalf run finalizes, a researchPrime / lane job finishes, or a Foreman wave GOes, one row is appended; Statement — a Foreman execution log appears as a clickable link
message: Criterion 1 names three finish events. The plan then (a) filters Hook B to `lane in ('research','plan')` so a classic build job writes nothing, (b) registers the execution log only on commissioned `finish_run` (Hook C), and (c) parks the only wave-GO writer (P2.8) behind a Stage-2 question. A Foreman run from the project window — the path the risk table itself keeps in scope — still leaves the outline and the tile empty. Per-wave GO never mints a row. Asking John to re-decide a locked criterion is not a HOLD of extra machinery; the third named finish event is still fiction. Commit a Foreman writer on the paths criterion 1 named, or amend the North Star.

criterion: 1 — the row carries the roadmap step it belongs to (the active step at the time); 3 — the plan outline's step expansion lists the step's register rows
message: The surface he locked is: open the roadmap step, click the report. Wave 3 will fill Step from `active_step` when the hint is omitted — at register time, after finalize. Hook C stamps the commission's step at launch. Hook A (Gandalf, the leading example) and Hook B pass no hint. If the step is no longer `active` when the hook fires — already done, or the next step now active — the row lands under the wrong step or under none. Wave 4's Gandalf Given/When/Then never asserts the Step cell at all, so Foreman can ship the named path with an outline join that the tile hides. Stamp the step at launch (Hook C already does), and assert it on the Gandalf fixture.

criterion: 4 — the command staged as a pending paste, Enter runs it; 5 — Playwright shows the command sitting unsent on the prompt
message: Criterion 4/5 require a clean command on the prompt so Enter runs it. For `backend=='shell'` the flush is "the PTY produced its first output bytes." A Windows PowerShell/`COMSPEC` banner is output that is not a prompt. Flushing raw command bytes into the banner means he does not see a staged line — and may not have a runnable command on the prompt at all. The existing greet-gated flush exists because "any output" is the wrong gate. Wave 5's stub PTY has no banner; Wave 7's live screenshot will either fail honestly or be skipped (Finding 2). Name an idle-prompt detector before claiming Enter-to-run.

criterion: 4 — a cockpit terminal in the project's tree with the command staged, Enter to run
message: The locked Run behavior is a terminal in the project's tree. Wave 5 hedges "project tree or a caller-supplied effort dir"; Wave 6 then sets cwd to "that row's effort dir when the row is effort-level." A `run: python tools/foo.py` written against the project root fails on Enter when cwd is `planning/…/effort`. He pressed Enter; it did not run. That is the operator failure criterion 4 exists to prevent. Allowlist the command; cwd is the project folder the North Star named, unless the row itself declares otherwise.

criterion: 3 — a report registered with a step shows in the plan outline; the deliverables tile always shows it
message: The risk table sends a run with no effort to the project root. Hook B does not call `effort_dir_for`. It uses `rec.get('effort_dir') or project root`, and the `effort_dir` passthrough is optional with "no behavior change when absent" and no caller named. The plan outline reads the effort's `DELIVERABLES.md`. A project that has an effort — the case he works in — then shows the classic-window report in the project-root list, not under the step he opens. Criterion 3 is both places, not "whichever file the project-wide pane happens to read." Wire the passthrough on the launch paths that have an effort, or those reports stay missing from the outline.

criterion: 1 — a finished run registers itself (one row is appended); 5 — it is seen
message: Criterion 1 is a row appearing; criterion 5 is that he can click it. `register()` never raises; the only observer of `written:false` is a journal field `{register: written|dup|reason}` he does not read. A finish that no-ops leaves the outline and the tile exactly as they are today — no link — with no cockpit signal. Best-effort is right (a registrar exception must not fail the job). Operator-visible success cannot be only a journal field. Surface the miss on the effort, or fail the Wave 7 dogfood when the row is absent; otherwise "it is seen" is unenforceable the first time a hook no-ops in production.

criterion: 1 — when a researchPrime / lane job finishes, one row is appended
message: Idempotency is on exact `(what, where)`. Hook B writes `'<researchPrime|Crucible> <lane> report — <label>'` at `/report/<pid>/<lane>/<job_id>`. Hook C writes `'<skill> — <role>: <filename>'` at the session-doc path. A commissioned researchPrime that also `_finalize`s a lane job is one run minting two rows with two labels and two Wheres. He opens the step and sees the same report twice. The plan never says Hook B skips commissioned jobs. One finish event, one row — pick a writer per path, or the register stops being a click target.

criterion: 3 — Both places, one source — the pane and the plan outline render the same register rows as links
message: The register is one source; the paint is still two. `delivRow` emits the tokenized `<a target=_blank>`. `loadDeliv` gets a separate `window.open(route + token)` branch. The plan already admits that leaving `loadDeliv` unpatched makes the same row a link in the tile and dead text in the other list. That failure returns the day the copies diverge. Make `loadDeliv` call `delivRow` (or one helper). Two hand-kept route branches are how one of the two places goes dark.

criterion: 4 — a Run link opens … an Anchor window (a cockpit terminal in the project's tree)
message: He clicks Run ▶ and, if the alias is cut, lands on the existing standalone page behind `/zombie_terminal` — a window whose object is Zombie Hunter, not the command he just staged. The HOLD's question is already answered by that page taking `session`+`token`. A second route to the same page retires nothing. If the existing URL is used, retitle by session kind; do not ship a Run control that opens the hunter.

criterion: 1 — When a Gandalf run finalizes, a researchPrime / lane job finishes, or a Foreman wave GOes, one row is appended
section: Wave 4 — Hook B/C and HOLD P2.8
message: Criterion 1 names three finish events. The third is not “Foreman finishes.” It is “a Foreman wave GOes.” The plan parks that trigger (P2.8, “NOT built by default — folded into Hook C”) and then excludes the build lane from Hook B (`lane in ('research', 'plan')` only). What remains is a commissioned RUN_DONE row for an execution log, once, if the session was steward-commissioned. A five-wave build that GOes four times and then dies never fires finish_run, so the register is empty for the whole life of the run — the opposite of the locked trigger. The risk row already decided the classic-window case (project root is the effort of record). Hook B refusing `build` plus P2.8 HOLD together leave that mitigation unimplemented. Re-asking “live per-wave or once at finish?” at the Stage-2 gate re-opens a lock. Wire the wave-GO row, or amend criterion 1. As written, the third trigger is neither implementable nor measured.

criterion: 2 — a register row may point at an Anchor route, not only an in-effort file; 5 — a Gandalf run on a real project is opened from the plan outline AND the deliverables tile
message: The Why Now is that the register already opens files inside the effort folder and fails on reports that live in lane output dirs and Gandalf run dirs. Wave 4 then states that a cockpit-commissioned Gandalf store IS the effort dir, so Where is the plain `gandalf/run-<id>/report.md` — today’s realpath containment, already a link. Wave 7 dogfoods exactly that path and asserts a click through to “Bottom line.” That screenshot can be taken on the current parser with classify_route never succeeding. The new Where forms the plan exists to add — `/artifact/<pid>?path=…` for an out-of-effort report, `/report/<pid>/<lane>/<job_id>` for a lane job — are not the live click. Criterion 2 is therefore identified by a source-level delivRow assertion (Wave 2) and never by the page criterion 5 names. A green W7 on a commissioned in-effort Gandalf does not falsify “skill reports still render as text.”

criterion: 5 — Nothing regresses, and it is seen; the steward/cockpit nets stay green
message: The machine-countable gate is `tests/test_steward_deliverables.py`, two pre-existing cockpit files, and `tests/test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`. No wave creates `test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`. The files the waves do emit — `test_register_routes_2026_09_05.py`, `test_deliverables_register_2026_09_05.py`, `test_run_deliverable_terminal.py`, `test_register_links_playwright_2026_09_05.py` — are absent from that command. Foreman either collection-fails on a missing file or, if someone adds an empty namesake, never runs the STUB GATE, the registrar concurrency/idempotency net, the Run allowlist, or the only page proof. Criterion 5’s “nets stay green” is then a count over the wrong tests. A gate that cannot emit counts for the claims it ships is not a gate.

criterion: 5 — a Gandalf run opened from outline AND tile; a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged (Playwright screenshots), before v1.2.13
message: Criterion 5 is a claim about the page, not about pytest staying green. The only surface proof is `tests/test_register_links_playwright_2026_09_05.py` with `pytest.importorskip('playwright')`, and that file is not in the plan test-command. importorskip means the steward/cockpit/terminal nets named in the same criterion can pass while Playwright never ran. The run: half plants a hand-written smoke row — it does not observe a finish hook writing `run:` — so a screenshot of a staged command does not identify criterion 1 and criterion 4 together. File-presence of a PNG is the v4 failure class this wave cites and then reimplements. Name a non-skippable ship rule that the two clicks and the unsent command are on the page, or criterion 5 remains a procedure.

criterion: 2 — a Where cell that is /report/… or /artifact/… is openable; the pane and the plan outline render it as a link that opens in a new window
message: Wave 1’s positive fixture is `/artifact/<pid>?path=gandalf/run-1/report.md` and the grammar forbids a second query key on the stored cell. Wave 2 then sets `href` to “the route plus the token appended exactly as the deliverable-file link does at :458–462.” File-link concatenation and a pre-formed `/artifact/…?path=` URL are not the same shape. Naive `?token=` on a route that already has `?path=` yields a URL the artifact handler will not open; `&token=` is a second query key the parser would reject if it were stored. The Wave 2 test (“href is the route plus the page token”) passes either join. No assertion requires a single well-formed query string that `/artifact/` accepts. Criterion 2’s “opens in a new window” is therefore not identified for the route form the Why Now actually needs.

criterion: 1 — one row is appended when a run finishes; Double rows on retry/resume — registrar idempotent on (what, where)
section: Wave 4 — Hook B and Hook C
message: Idempotency is exact `(what, where)`. Hook B writes `/report/<pid>/<lane>/<job_id>` with a lane-job what-string. Hook C writes a different where (in-effort rel or `/artifact/…`) and a different what (`<skill> — <role>: <filename>`). The plan never states these finish points are mutually exclusive, and a commissioned researchPrime/Crucible run is the production path that can be both a lane job and a `finish_run`. Tests pin “`_finalize` twice” and “`finish_run` twice,” each hook against itself. They do not pin one commissioned finish → one row across both hooks. Two where values are two rows. Criterion 1’s count is then unmeasured on the steward path the elegance pass calls load-bearing.

criterion: 1 — one row is appended when a run finishes
message: Criterion 1 is a count: one row per named finish. Hook B obeys it (one `/report/` per job). Hook C does not: done-when is “exactly one row per human-facing doc.” A session with report + plan + execlog is three rows for one RUN_DONE. Idempotency on `(what, where)` cannot collapse that grain because each file is a different where. The North Star’s examples are a Gandalf report, a researchPrime plan or report, a Foreman execution log — one human artifact per finish, not a role map. The plan therefore cannot say what “one row” means on the commissioned path. Pick a grain — one row per finished run, pointing at the human artifact — and gate it; the blast is not that grain.

criterion: 1 — when a run finalizes, one row is appended to the effort’s DELIVERABLES.md
message: The Why Now is that listing a human artifact is a hope because nothing writes the row. The fix is a function that “never raises (best-effort, returns the reason)” plus a journal field `{register: written|dup|reason}` and “a registrar exception can never fail a finished run.” A successful Gandalf/lane/commission finish can therefore still leave DELIVERABLES.md unchanged, and the surface John reads (outline + tile) has no failure state — only a log line. Tests pin cancelled/failed → no row and duplicate → one row; they do not pin “STATUS_DONE + `written: false`” as a visible miss. Journaling a silent no-op makes the miss auditable, not true. Criterion 1 is not “we tried.” Until a successful run with a failed write is a failed surface (or a hard, retried write), the convention remains a hope with better logs.

criterion: 4 — Run link opens a cockpit terminal with the command staged as a pending paste (Enter runs it); 5 — a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged
message: The dependent variable is the command sitting unsent on the shell prompt so Enter runs it. The plan operationalizes “prompt” as “the PTY produced its first output bytes.” First bytes from `%COMSPEC%`/PowerShell are banner, profile, or a cwd warning — not `PS …>`. Flushing raw bytes into that stream (explicitly no bracketed paste, no trailing newline) can land the command in the middle of startup text; Enter then does not run the staged command as a unit, which is a failure mode the risk table (“never submits”) does not name. The stub PTY “emits immediately,” so the once-only / no-newline fixtures cannot see a real prompt. The 45-second greet fallback is removed as an auto-send hazard and not replaced, so a quiet shell never stages at all. Criterion 4 is identified against a stub that cannot fail the way the host shell fails.

criterion: 3 argument is “stepDelivLine already calls delivRow … zero outline-side edits … hence in the deliverables tile and under its step.” The Given/When/Then claims a cockpit render of step 2’s expansion. The tests actually listed are API pass-through and a jsdom-free source scan for `innerHTML`. If stepDelivLine (or anything upstream) still filters on `it.path` / in-effort existence, route rows vanish from the outline while delivRow unit tests stay green. Wave 3 keys Step as a 1-based index of `status == 'active'`; that join is asserted against a synthetic map, not against `stepDelivLine`’s real key. Criterion 3 is a join on the page. This wave measures a renderer helper and a comment about reuse.

criterion: 4 — Run link opens a cockpit terminal in an Anchor window, token-gated, killable
message: Criterion 4 is the window. Wave 6 leaves the URL as a HOLD (“can window.open reach the existing standalone xterm page with session+token as-is? If yes, cut the alias”). That is an unclosed decision inside a wave this document calls Foreman-ready. The existing page is already served at `/zombie_terminal?session=&token=`; a second route to the same page retires nothing. Wave 7’s Playwright cannot be written until the href is locked, so the surface gate depends on a question the plan deferred. Lock the URL or cut the alias. Do not ship a HOLD as the Run window.

criterion: 1 — one row is appended; Double rows on retry/resume — registrar idempotent on (what, where)
message: The plan cites the WinError-5 cross-process replace race and claims durability via unique temp + `os.replace` under `WRITE_LOCK`. The emitted property gate requires temp + fsync + rename and “two real processes.” Wave 3 specifies no fsync and tests “two-thread register → one row.” Threads in one process do not identify the incident the unique tmp name exists for, and they cannot see a torn replace across two finish hooks in two processes. Idempotency under the lock they share is a different claim. The durability story and the test measure different machines.
